title: Mushroom Marsala Spaghetti
cScaleSummary: C0 because the recipe contains no cholesterol-contributing animal-derived ingredients. The mushrooms, pasta, olive oil, Marsala wine, herbs, aromatics, vegetable stock, and seasonings contribute 0 mg cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active is false because the recipe is designed primarily around classic pasta and pan-sauce structure rather than LDL-lowering ingredients or legume-forward composition, even though it remains low in cholesterol.
intro: Marsala sauce is closely tied to Italian-American restaurant cooking, especially veal Marsala, where browned meat, mushrooms, fortified wine, and pan reduction become a glossy savory sauce. This pasta keeps that familiar Marsala direction but lets mushrooms carry the dish. The sauce should be deep, wine-dark, and savory, clinging to thin spaghetti through reduction, pasta starch, and hard browning.

stepGroups.title: Brown the mushrooms
items: Heat a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Add half of the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-mushrooms}}) and half of the mushrooms ({{quantity:cremini-mushrooms}}).
Spread the mushrooms into an even layer and cook without stirring until deeply browned on the first side, about 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir and continue cooking until the mushrooms are browned, reduced, and no longer watery, about 5 to 6 minutes more.
Season with half of the kosher salt ({{quantity:kosher-salt-mushrooms}}) and half of the black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper-mushrooms}}).
Transfer the browned mushrooms to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining olive oil, mushrooms, kosher salt, and black pepper.

stepGroups.title: Build the sauce
items: Reduce the heat to medium and add the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-sauce}}).
Add the shallot ({{quantity:shallot}}) and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic ({{quantity:garlic}}) and thyme ({{quantity:thyme}}). Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste ({{quantity:tomato-paste}}) and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens slightly and coats the shallot-garlic base.
Add the Marsala wine ({{quantity:dry-marsala}}) and scrape the pan thoroughly to release the browned mushroom fond.
Simmer until the Marsala is reduced by about half and smells rounded rather than sharp, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Add the vegetable stock ({{quantity:vegetable-stock}}), soy sauce ({{quantity:soy-sauce}}), and black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper-sauce}}).
Return the mushrooms to the skillet and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until the sauce is savory and lightly reduced.

stepGroups.title: Cook the pasta
items: Bring the water ({{quantity:water}}) to a boil.
Add the kosher salt ({{quantity:kosher-salt-pasta}}) and thin spaghetti ({{quantity:thin-spaghetti}}).
Cook until the pasta is just shy of al dente.
Reserve 1 cup pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.

stepGroups.title: Finish the pasta
items: Add the thin spaghetti directly to the mushroom Marsala sauce.
Toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, adding small splashes of pasta water as needed, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the pasta.
Turn off the heat.
Stir in the lemon juice ({{quantity:lemon-juice}}) and parsley ({{quantity:parsley}}).
Let the pasta rest for 2 minutes before serving so the sauce settles onto the spaghetti.
